rules.name: Subgroup criterion
rules.input_form: nonempty subset H of a group G
preconditions: H is nonempty
rules.operation: Use the one-step subgroup test based on closure under ab^(-1).
examples: Closure under the subgroup test verifies many candidate subgroups efficiently
counterexamples: Checking only closure under multiplication without inverses is insufficient in general

rules.name: Homomorphism preservation rule
preconditions: The map is declared in an algebraic category with specified operations
rules.operation: Preserve the active algebraic operations under a homomorphism.
examples: Group homomorphisms send products to products and identities to identities
counterexamples: Arbitrary set maps need not preserve structure

rules.name: Ideal criterion in a ring
rules.input_form: subset I of a ring R
preconditions: R is a ring with the declared operations
rules.operation: Classify a subset as an ideal via additive subgroup and absorption conditions.
examples: Multiples of a fixed integer form an ideal in the integer ring
counterexamples: Additive closure alone without absorption is insufficient for ideal status

rules.name: Field nonzero invertibility rule
preconditions: a is nonzero in the active field
rules.operation: Use field structure to invert any nonzero element.
examples: Rational numbers form a field because every nonzero rational has a reciprocal in Q
counterexamples: Zero does not admit a multiplicative inverse in a field

rules.name: First isomorphism theorem seed
rules.output_form: domain modulo kernel(phi) isomorphic to image(phi)
preconditions: phi is a well-defined homomorphism in the active algebraic category
rules.operation: Collapse kernel-equivalent elements to obtain the image through a quotient-isomorphism statement.
examples: Quotienting out the kernel compresses exactly the redundancy of the homomorphism
counterexamples: Replacing the kernel by an arbitrary subset is invalid

rules.name: Normal subgroup criterion
rules.output_form: gNg^(-1) = N for all g in G
preconditions: N is already known to be a subgroup of G
rules.operation: Check normality by conjugation invariance.
examples: Kernels of group homomorphisms are normal subgroups
counterexamples: An arbitrary subgroup need not be normal

rules.name: Quotient group operation rule
rules.input_form: cosets aN and bN with N normal
preconditions: N is a normal subgroup of G
rules.operation: Define group multiplication on cosets after normality ensures well-definedness.
examples: Quotient groups inherit a well-defined multiplication only after normality is established
counterexamples: Defining coset multiplication for nonnormal subgroups is invalid in general

rules.name: Cyclic subgroup generator rule
rules.output_form: subgroup generated by integer powers or integer multiples of a
preconditions: The active notation convention for the algebraic operation is fixed
rules.operation: Generate a cyclic subgroup from a single element.
examples: Cyclic subgroups are determined entirely by one generator element
counterexamples: Adding unrelated elements to the generated set is invalid

rules.name: Irreducibility seed over a field
rules.output_form: irreducible iff no nontrivial factorization exists over that field
preconditions: A coefficient field is fixed
rules.operation: Classify polynomial irreducibility relative to the active coefficient field.
examples: Irreducibility depends on the coefficient field, not just the formal expression
counterexamples: Calling a polynomial irreducible over every field after checking only one field is invalid

rules.name: Principal ideal rule in a PID
rules.input_form: ideal I in a principal ideal domain
preconditions: The ambient ring is a principal ideal domain
rules.operation: Collapse ideals to single generators in a PID.
examples: Ideals in the integers are generated by one integer
counterexamples: Extending the rule automatically to arbitrary integral domains is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
